item.title: How Americans see China now
item.description: As President Trump heads to China this week, a new NPR-Chicago Council-Ipsos poll finds most Americans think U.S. tariffs have hurt both economies, and that the Iran war is bad for America.

item.title: Israel's government is expected to collapse over ultra-Orthodox military draft
item.description: An ultra-Orthodox Jewish party in Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition has called for parliament to be dissolved, threatening to bring down the government.

item.title: Trump expected to talk Iran and trade during summit in China
item.description: President Trump arrives in China Wednesday for a summit with his Chinese counterpart, where the war in Iran, trade policies and Taiwan are expected to be major points of discussion.

item.title: Putin hails Russia's test launch of a new ballistic missile
item.description: Russia test-fired a new intercontinental ballistic missile as part of efforts to modernize its nuclear forces. The nuclear-armed Sarmat missile would enter combat service at the end of the year.

item.title: The war is on hold, but Iran’s internal crackdown is only deepening
item.description: While the Iranian regime has been battling its external enemies, Israel and the United States, it has also been ramping up a deadly crackdown on those seen as the enemy within.

item.title: War in Iran costs $29 billion so far. And, students are finally improving in math
item.description: Pentagon officials told Congress they estimate the war in Iran has cost $29 billion so far. And, a new Education Scorecard shows U.S. students are improving in math.

item.title: Japanese snack packages turning black-and-white as Iran war depletes ink supply
item.description: The packaging on some snacks is turning black-and-white, as the war in Iran disrupts the supply of an ingredient used in colored ink. Calbee's chips originally came in a bright-orange bag.

item.title: An intimate look at one military family's life on pause as the Iran war continues
item.description: Military life has always involved some degree of uncertainty. But for many families, the fear and unknowns that come with the Iran war are new territory.
